I'm tired of it and for that reason, I'm going to cut to the chase:

Anyone who looks at any issue for which there is insufficient evidence to support any specific conclusion then goes ahead and picks one or another position and invests belief in it anyway is irrational at best.

Belief counts for absolutely nothing. It's an entirely internal aberration - a flaw in reasoning that leads people to treat pretend knowledge as if it's a legitimate substitute for real knowledge.

Those who self-describe as agnostics most often do so specifically because they don't fall into that mental trap - because they have sufficient intellectual integrity not only to accept the self-evident fact that the only objectively supportable position regarding an issue on which there is no certain knowledge is "I don't know," but to recognize that pretending otherwise merely invites irrationality.
